title: Tool capability recipe (self-evolution capabilities/ library, DECLARED plane)
description: A recipe for acquiring + health-checking ONE analysis/build tool capability. This library is fully independent of the experience knowledge base: it has its own status machine and validator and shares only library-level primitives (ConvertTo-CanonicalJson / Get-StringSha256 / Get-PublicContentFindings). TWO-PLANE STORAGE: this schema describes the DECLARED plane (capabilities/recipes/, committed) which records WHAT WE APPROVED and accepts only status proposed|approved. Runtime facts (installed/verified/quarantined, measured hashes, selftest evidence, install root) live in the machine-local runtime plane and are never committed -- so a committed file can never be edited into a usable state. A recipe records how a tool is (a) fetched as a single hashable artifact, extracted inertly (never running an installer/in-package script), byte-bound by hash and re-hashed at use time, and (b) health-checked by a closed machine predicate with a mandatory negative sample. A green selftest only proves the tool is HEALTHY/available -- never that a target's original behaviour was reproduced; per-target ANALYSIS-FINDINGS / RUN-EVIDENCE stay mandatory.

tool_capability_id.description: Stable id of the tool capability, e.g. unpack.pe.upx / decompile.dotnet / build.rust. Named tool_capability_id (not capability) so it never collides with the source track's product CAPABILITY-MAP.

status.description: Declared-plane status only. proposed=recorded, not human-approved; approved=approved out-of-band against a specific payload (see approval). installed/verified/quarantined are RUNTIME facts and are refused in this plane by the validator -- they live in the machine-local runtime plane.

target_strength.description: Whether the recipe implies a target can be reproduced. A tool-health selftest can only ever yield UNVERIFIED, so UNVERIFIED is the only accepted value and a target-verified badge cannot be set at all. Per-target reproduction still requires ANALYSIS-FINDINGS / RUN-EVIDENCE. Covered by payload_sha256 so the claim cannot be raised after approval.

acquire.description: How the single hashable artifact is fetched. NEVER an installer/winget/git/free command -- those are excluded from the auto path (manual out-of-band only). Extraction is done ONLY by our own code (Expand-Archive / System.IO.Compression); no in-package script is executed.

source_url.description: HTTPS official source. No userinfo, no ?token/?key, no embedded absolute path.

expected_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the DOWNLOADED artifact itself (the zip or the exe), pinned by us -- never trusted from a platform digest field.

hash_source.description: Provenance of expected_sha256, strongest first. tofu_first_measured means trust-on-first-use: we measured it ourselves once with nothing to compare against. Without this field a TOFU hash is byte-identical in the library to a publisher-published one, and the phase-C batch pre-approval would silently grant it the same trust. tofu_first_measured may NEVER ride the auto-approval path (per-entry human approval only) and may not be combined with a signer. Covered by payload_sha256 so the tier cannot be silently upgraded.

signer.description: Authenticode signer expectation when the artifact is validly signed. Mutually exclusive with unsigned_ack=true: declaring both is a contradictory provenance claim and is refused. A bare subject string is not enough -- phase C needs a machine-checkable match policy, and an untimestamped signature on a pinned old version is a time bomb that must be visible.

subject_exact.description: Full expected subject, required when match_policy=subject_exact.

org.description: Expected organisation, required when match_policy=org. Use this rather than subject_exact where a publisher legitimately signs under several subjects.

status.description: Expected Get-AuthenticodeSignature status, so the phase-C check is a machine comparison rather than a string guess.

timestamped.description: Whether the signature carries a trusted countersignature timestamp. False means the pinned version stops validating once the signing cert expires.

unsigned_ack.description: True iff the tool is legitimately unsigned (e.g. diec/go/cargo/rustc). When true, unsigned_reason is required, signer must be absent, and the pinned hashes are the integrity anchor in place of a signature.

entry_relpath.description: Relative path, inside the extracted artifact, of the exe actually invoked (for artifact_type=exe this is the artifact itself). No absolute path, no drive letter, no parent traversal.

entry_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the entry exe after inert extraction. Re-hashed before every invocation (anti-TOCTOU); a mismatch quarantines the recipe.

verify.description: Tool-health selftest: a CLOSED machine predicate judged by the script (never by an LLM), with a mandatory negative sample. expected_output_assert is written from a known-answer fixture, never back-filled from the tool's live output. Both samples must exist under fixtures/capabilities/ and hash to the recorded value -- the validator checks the files on disk.

invoke_command.description: How the selftest runs the tool. Relative/env-var only; no absolute path.

expected_output_assert.description: Closed predicate over the tool output on the positive sample.

selftest_sample.description: Relative path, under fixtures/capabilities/, to a legal, publicly-shareable, known-answer positive fixture. Must exist and match selftest_sample_sha256.

negative_sample.description: A sample under fixtures/capabilities/ that the tool MUST reject / return empty on -- guards against a stub that always returns the same answer. Must exist and match negative_sample_sha256.

approval.description: Records WHICH payload a human approved. Required at status=approved, forbidden at status=proposed. approval.payload_sha256 must equal the recomputed payload hash, so changing any safety field invalidates the approval even if the editor dutifully refreshes payload_sha256 -- without this block payload_sha256 is only a checksum, not an approval anchor.

payload_sha256.description: Integrity hash covering EVERY safety-critical field (tool_capability_id, target_strength, acquire.source_url/pinned_version/artifact_type/expected_sha256/hash_source/signer/unsigned_ack/entry_relpath/entry_sha256, verify.invoke_command/expected_output_assert + the sample hashes). status is deliberately excluded because it advances legitimately; it is constrained instead by the plane rule and by approval.
